how: The opening gives members a logo project and a location to work on.
The starter proposes the mark and location, fitting the revised role without making others joining part of that role.
Members revise the letter O and consider larger or different series marks after the first completion report.
A proposed letter revision combines reported assent from the opening author with an invitation for other members to object.
Members report progress and announce that the logo is done.
An anchor coordinate and a direct canvas link locate the work without establishing a complete pixel template.
A participant judges taking new territory difficult because available numbers barely suffice to hold the existing work.
A newcomer receives an explanation of the event and thanks the explainer after completion has already been announced.
Completion announcements precede the newcomer's request for explanation, without showing that completion caused the question.
Reported assent from the opening author does not establish formal appointment, and one room cannot test the model's cross-room prevalence claim.
Participants describe difficulty holding existing work and turn a completion celebration into a call to defend it.
Apply P05 here to holding and defense calls; whether keepers erased agreed changes or failed to receive a revision remains unresolved.
Members attribute a crooked box and repeated intrusive dots to a neighbour without independently tracing the placers.
The starter explicitly tells members to spare the banner of a neighbour described as an ally.
The stated reason for restraint is ally status, while a different neighbour's alleged encroachment receives a retaliatory proposal.
Internal talk establishes unilateral border management, while interpreting it as negotiated settlement requires a neighbour's response that this record does not supply.
A member proposes making the neighbour's border crooked, another commits, and another justifies entering its space.
A repair request receives retaliatory border alteration as an alternative, making conflict a direct branch of maintenance talk.
A different spot is proposed, but the response favors holding existing work and the final exchange confirms survival without documenting a move.
Completion reports, celebratory gestures and admiration publicly mark the shared work as an achievement.
Members report the imperfect result, confirm survival and identify the logo in the final canvas.
Preserving a small work's outcome includes helping a viewer locate it inside the crowded final image.
The final exchange locates and celebrates the logo without revealing whether members later reused it or continued the collective effort.
Explaining the ordinary pixel interval does not establish whether anyone used scripts, bots or spare accounts.
Bare assent answers the retaliatory border proposal, while the coordinate reply and newcomer's thanks show other one-line answers.
One participant reports working on another room's symbol, establishing individual cross-work help without establishing returned support for this room.
Calling neighbours allies and expecting support does not show coalition formation, mutual commitments or shared defense.
Celebrating the room's completed work does not establish a rival-directed taunt, victory claim or other continuing contest in talk.
Building beneath an ally's mark establishes proximity without demonstrating guest tenure under that neighbour's rule.
The ally reminder and expected support do not identify an envoy carrying proposals between rooms.
The project post does not demonstrate host moderation, canvas containment or suspension of ordinary activities.
Calling the site event April Fools does not establish a host-sub prank or a joke project call.
The explicit reason offered for invading concerns recent pixel interference rather than a recorded quarrel predating the canvas.
Series-specific image proposals show representation without establishing a prior quarrel, ideological argument, running joke or colour doctrine carried into the conflict.
The incursion justification cites recent interference and occupation, leaving a pre-canvas tie naming the rival unobserved.
The ally reminder establishes neither a dispute over binding authority nor a statement limiting who may commit members to an agreement.
The final-version question checks survival and location rather than contesting cleanup, correcting a historical claim or choosing a preserved version.
A Discord-hosted reference image and reported OP assent do not establish a move of planning into chat or a chat decision brought back.
Asking what the canvas is does not establish that the mark brought the speaker into the room.
Saying the O resembles a zero motivates a design revision without establishing a shared pun or running canvas joke.
The room selects an initial spot and considers another to avoid conflict, without documenting prior destruction or an executed relocation.
The project call does not establish a new room forming around the mark.
The incursion justification does not establish an argument over offensive language, slurs or hate symbols.
Admiration for the finished logo does not establish seeking creators' notice or press attention outside the canvas.
A member justifies invading the neighbour by repeated interference and recent occupation, a local argument for acceptable encroachment rather than a general canvas philosophy.
Disappointment with the mark's scale does not establish withdrawal under personal strain or a quarrel repaired between members.
The visible coordinate and design exchange does not establish secret planning, infiltration or reaching into rivals' venues.
The project opening does not establish opposition to canvas posts leading members to attack their own mark.
Predicting opponents' sleep does not establish that this room's members fitted their own placing around sleep, work or device access.
Explaining the standard pixel interval does not establish site faults, exceptional timers or fixes.
Working on another fandom's symbol does not establish dual membership in this border contest or reassurance about divided loyalties.
Progress reports follow the opening call, but the record does not identify the call's causal contribution to members' placements.
The starter proposal and initial call occupy one passage, preventing a distinct starter-then-call sequence from being established.
An explicit defense call follows completion and celebration, naming the finished mark as something now needing protection.
Repair talk elicits internal retaliation, but no neighbour's negotiating turn establishes the proposed upkeep-to-bilateral-border-talk mechanism.
Restraint is explicitly explained by ally status, while an earlier negotiation producing that restraint is not recorded.
Holding difficulty and a defense call do not reveal whether members turned to automation.
The completion announcement receives a celebratory reply, while an earlier announcement combines reporting and celebration in the same passage.
Celebration precedes final-image checking, but the stated problem is locating the small mark, so the record supports sequence without establishing celebration as its cause.
Finding and celebrating the final image cannot establish whether recording caused later reuse or collective continuation outside the supplied window.
Low numbers can motivate holding existing work instead of moving, so applying the move arrow requires evidence of loss and adopted relocation beyond capacity doubts alone.
Coordinates precede the proposed O revision, and the linked reference image does not establish a later agreed pixel template settling that revision.
The opening project proposal receives a one-line answer assenting and supplying the direct canvas location.
The retaliatory border proposal also receives bare assent, supplying an attack-to-acceptance branch alongside constructive call-and-answer.
Expected allied support and a holding problem do not establish a strain-driven request followed by help from another room.
Neither the ally reminder nor the border conflict records a negotiated exchange of help for space or protection.
Recruitment precedes retaliation, but the direct reply links the attack proposal to a crooked-border repair problem rather than establishing recruitment as its cause.
In the fully recorded attack-proposal response branch, both answers assent or justify invasion rather than refusing, restraining or apologizing.
The attack proposal's recorded answers commit to action and justify invasion without invoking a truce or proposing a deal.
Assenting to and justifying the attack proposal do not establish a subsequent rival-directed contest in talk.
Named allies and expected support do not reveal when any alliance formed or whether defense needs produced it.
The logo call supplies no evidence of the proposed flood of canvas posts and ensuing host containment.
Even with the revised bounds, the ally reminder establishes neither agreement-making nor a limit on binding authority through which this arrow could be tested.
